subject: SAC-B4 reversible familiarity modulation

biologicalReference.citation: Hattori et al. (2017), Representations of Novelty and Familiarity in a Mushroom Body Compartment, Cell 169(5):956-969.e17
biologicalReference.engineeringReading: Repeated exposure to the same odor rapidly suppresses novelty-related activity in the studied mushroom-body compartment. SEI uses this only as inspiration for temporary attenuation of stable repeated caller-identified events.

firstSlice.placement: prototype-go/familiarity reusable evaluation helper; not wired into current SUI provider or CLI

syntheticObservations.observation: Attenuation begins only at the configured repeat threshold.
Caller-visible fingerprint delta immediately restores full attention and resets repetition.
A gap equal to ExpiryTicks restores full attention in the first slice.
High-stakes restores one observation without erasing familiarity state; provenance is required.

syntheticObservations.scenario: Underlying content changes but caller continues to provide the same fingerprint.
syntheticObservations.observation: The familiarity layer cannot detect a change omitted from the caller-owned fingerprint. This is the primary missed-change failure boundary.
Oldest entry is evicted; equal-tick ties are resolved deterministically by lexical key order.

localVerification.method: A temporary module used the same familiarity helper source and equivalent focused tests for policy validation, repeat attenuation, delta/expiry/stakes recovery, ineligible bypass, hidden-fingerprint change risk, deterministic eviction, monotonic logical time, and reproducibility.

benchmark.subject: repeated same-key/same-fingerprint Observe hot path after initialization
benchmark.note: Temporary-module microbenchmark only; not a full repository checkout, Go 1.25 result, or production performance guarantee.
